Consult Summary:
- Young adult female with a 3-day history of a severe, continuous headache with photophobia and intermittent visual "shooting light" phenomena; appointment arranged for neurological exam and fundoscopy; symptomatic analgesic treatment offered.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden onset headache 3 days ago; persistent, described as "blinding" and impairing concentration and work.
- Onset/duration/progression: Woke with headache three days ago; continuous, partially responsive to ibuprofen but not fully relieved.
- Pain characteristics: Generalized, more intense over the right eye; severity reported ~8/10 at worst, decreases to ~5/10 with analgesia.
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia (light sensitivity); intermittent visual phenomena described as "shooting light" or "weird kind of vision"; feeling "a bit sick" but no vomiting.
- Negative findings: No nausea/vomiting (explicitly no vomiting), no focal weakness, no numbness/tingling, no change in smell/taste, no fever reported, no recent upper respiratory or sinus symptoms, no epistaxis or hemoptysis.
- Temporal features/relief factors: Some reduction with ibuprofen; not waking patient at night; can be worse briefly when standing up quickly or with abrupt head movements (stabbing sensation).
- Past headache history: Occasional short headaches previously (up to ~2 days) responsive to ibuprofen; one childhood episode investigated with no cause found.
- Past medical history / medications / allergies:
  - Contraceptive pill in use for ~1 year — specific preparation/name not documented.
  - Occasional ibuprofen use for headaches.
  - No other regular medications documented.
  - Allergies: patient reports none.
- Family history: Mother has migraines with vomiting.
- Social history / preventive care: Lives alone; works from home but has missed work; drinks alcohol ("probably like, three, once a week" — patient phrasing); does not smoke; blood pressure checked at pharmacy ~1 year ago and reported as normal.
- Recent eye check: Recent eye check reported with "nothing changed" in vision.

Examination:
- Vitals: not documented.
- Examination findings: none documented (neurological and fundoscopic exam not yet performed).

Impression:
- Possible migraine-type headache given photophobia and visual symptoms; persistent severe headache for 3 days warrants in-person neurological and fundoscopic examination to exclude other causes.

Plan:
- Arrange in-person appointment with support team for full neurological examination and fundoscopy; blood pressure to be checked during that visit.
- Symptomatic treatment offered:
  - Continue/try ibuprofen as needed (patient already using).
  - Prescribe a stronger analgesic "similar to ibuprofen" — name/dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Advised paracetamol can be taken concurrently — dose/route/frequency not documented.
  - Instruction: take prescribed medication with food.
- Contraception: continue current pill for now; suitability may be reassessed if migraine with aura is confirmed and may require change.
- Safety netting: If headache worsens, becomes unbearable, or changes in character, go to A&E for urgent assessment; patient advised to call for further advice as needed.
- If headache settles before appointment, in-person exam can be canceled.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing but expected clinical elements:
  - Vital signs (blood pressure, pulse, temperature).
  - Detailed neurological and fundoscopic examination findings.
  - Specific names, doses, routes, and frequencies for prescribed medication(s).
  - Exact contraceptive formulation.
  - Pregnancy status (not documented).
  - Medication reconciliation (complete list of regular/PRN meds).
- Internal conflicts from transcript:
  - None identified.
- Transcript quality:
  - Generally understandable; minor initial audio/volume issue resolved. Some patient responses were fragmented but clinically interpretable.
